newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat, Netanyahu to discuss implementing accord.
newsitem.headline: Arafat, Netanyahu to discuss implementing accord.

text.p: Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu and the Palestinians' Yasser Arafat meet at their border on Sunday to discuss expanding self-rule and the operation of Palestinian sea and air ports, officials said.
Prime Minister Netanyahu's office said the meeting would start at 1800 GMT at the Erez crossing to Gaza.
The Israeli leader put off the meeting, initially set for Thursday, after 73 Israeli soldiers died in the collision of two helicopters. It was Israel's worst military air disaster.

Israel was due to free 25 Palestinian women prisoners on Monday or Tuesday, officials for both sides said. Palestinian sources said they were all of the women prisoners among the 5,000 Palestinians held by Israel.

Chief Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said Arafat, the Palestinian president, wanted to discuss Israel's withdrawal of troops from West Bank rural areas planned for early March, the ports, and preparations for crucial "final-status" talks.
"We want to agree on preparations to resume final-status talks which should commence in the middle of next month," Erekat told Israel Radio.
The Palestinians also want to operate an airport in the southern Gaza Strip and build a seaport on the Mediterranean.

Erekat said Arafat would demand that Israel stop building Jewish settlements, confiscating Palestinian lands and revoking the residency of East Jerusalem Palestinians living outside the city boundaries.
In its last redeployment Israel withdrew its forces from 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron last month and agreed to discuss implementating other aspects of a self-rule deal signed in 1995.
Israel is committed to a three-stage army pullback from West Bank rural areas by mid-1998.
Netanyahu's aide David Bar Bar-Ilan told Reuters on Saturday night that all the "nitty-gritty" issues in the accord would be discussed as well as Israeli demands that the PLO respect its commitments.
"Prime Minister Netanyahu will obviously bring up the question of reciprocity regarding items included in the 'Note for the Record' which is attached to the Hebron agreement," Bar-Illan said.
The "Note for the Record" reaffirms the commitment by both sides to implement their 1995 interim peace deal and outlines the responsibilities of both the Israelis and Palestinians.
In it the Palestinians pledged to revise the Palestinian National Charter, which calls for the destruction of the state of Israel, and to fight terror.
Foreign Minister David Levy, recently appointed to lead Israel's negotiations with the PLO, will take part in Sunday's meeting with Arafat, a government spokesman said.
